Notes: Key points: Moses was tending his father-in-law's sheep at Horeb / A bush burned but was not consumed / God called Moses by name / God had seen the affliction of his people / God sent Moses to Pharaoh to bring the people out || Heart: When has God called you to a task you felt unready for? || Mission: Write down one thing God has asked you to do, and take one step towards it this week.

Question or prompt: The walls of Jericho
Notes: Key points: Jericho was shut up because of the Israelites / God told Joshua to march around the city / Seven priests carried trumpets of rams' horns / On the seventh day they marched seven times / The people shouted and the walls fell down || Heart: Where do you need to trust God's way of doing things, even when it seems strange? || Mission: Do one act of obedience this week that you have been putting off.

Question or prompt: Deborah and Barak
Notes: Key points: Deborah judged Israel under a palm tree / Deborah sent for Barak to fight Sisera / Sisera had nine hundred chariots of iron / Barak went to battle with Deborah / The LORD routed Sisera and his army || Heart: Who in your life has been a source of courage when you needed it? || Mission: Encourage someone this week who feels weak or afraid.

Question or prompt: Ruth's loyalty
Notes: Key points: Orpah kissed Naomi and went back / Ruth clung to Naomi / Ruth said where you go I will go / Ruth's people would be her people and her God her God / Naomi saw Ruth was determined and stopped speaking || Heart: What loyalty has God asked you to show to someone in your family or church? || Mission: Spend a practical hour this week helping someone who depends on you.

Question or prompt: Samuel's call
Notes: Key points: Samuel ministered to the LORD before Eli / The word of the LORD was rare in those days / The LORD called Samuel / Samuel thought Eli was calling him / Samuel answered: speak, for thy servant heareth || Heart: What helps you to listen for God's voice in your everyday life? || Mission: Set aside ten minutes each day this week to listen to God in silence or in Scripture.

Question or prompt: Nathan and David
Notes: Key points: The LORD sent Nathan to David / A rich man took a poor man's only ewe lamb / David was very angry with the rich man / Nathan said: Thou art the man / David confessed: I have sinned against the LORD || Heart: When has someone spoken truth to you that you needed to hear? || Mission: Ask a trusted friend this week to speak honestly with you about one area of your life.

Question or prompt: Solomon asks for wisdom
Notes: Key points: God appeared to Solomon in a dream / Solomon asked for an understanding heart / God was pleased with the request / God gave him wisdom and also riches and honour / God promised long life if he walked in his ways || Heart: What would you ask God for if he said, ask what I shall give thee? || Mission: Pray this week for wisdom in one decision you face, and read James 1:5 with a friend.

Question or prompt: The LORD is my shepherd
Notes: Key points: The LORD is my shepherd / I shall not want / He makes me lie down in green pastures / He leads me beside still waters / Even in the valley of the shadow of death I fear no evil / Goodness and mercy shall follow me || Heart: Which line of Psalm 23 comforts you most today, and why? || Mission: Learn Psalm 23 this month, and say it to someone who needs comfort.

Question or prompt: Isaiah's vision
Notes: Key points: Isaiah saw the Lord high and lifted up / Seraphims with six wings stood above / They cried holy, holy, holy / Isaiah said he was a man of unclean lips / A live coal from the altar touched his mouth / Isaiah answered: here am I, send me || Heart: What would it mean for you to say, here am I, send me, to God? || Mission: Tell God this week that you are willing to go wherever he sends you, and act on one opportunity.

Question or prompt: The Beatitudes
Notes: Key points: Jesus went up into a mountain and taught / Blessed are the poor in spirit / Blessed are the meek / Blessed are they that mourn / Blessed are the merciful / Blessed are the peacemakers || Heart: Which beatitude challenges you most, and why? || Mission: Do one act of mercy or peacemaking this week for someone who has hurt you or who is in need.

Question or prompt: Jesus calms the storm
Notes: Key points: The disciples were in a boat / A great storm of wind arose / Jesus was asleep on a pillow / The disciples woke him, saying they were perishing / Jesus rebuked the wind and said peace, be still / There was a great calm || Heart: What storm in your life do you need to bring to Jesus? || Mission: Tell one friend about a storm you have brought to Jesus, and pray for their storm this week.

Question or prompt: Jesus and the woman at the well
Notes: Key points: Jesus sat by Jacob's well / He asked the woman for a drink of water / The woman was surprised that a Jew spoke to her / Jesus spoke of living water / Whoever drinks will never thirst again || Heart: What does it mean to you that Jesus offers living water? || Mission: Thank Jesus each day this week for one way his grace has refreshed you.

Question or prompt: Saul's conversion
Notes: Key points: Saul breathed out threatenings and slaughter / A light from heaven shone round him / He fell to the ground and heard a voice: Saul, Saul / He was blind for three days / Ananias was sent to him / Something like scales fell from his eyes || Heart: Where has God changed your direction, as he changed Saul's? || Mission: Share the story of how God changed your life with one person this week.

Question or prompt: More than conquerors
Notes: Key points: All things work together for good for those who love God / Those called according to his purpose / Nothing can separate us from the love of Christ / Tribulation, distress, famine and sword are listed / Neither death nor life can separate us / We are more than conquerors || Heart: Which promise in Romans 8 do you most need to hear today? || Mission: Memorise Romans 8:38-39 this week, and recite it when you feel afraid.

Question or prompt: A new heaven and a new earth
Notes: Key points: John saw a new heaven and a new earth / The holy city, new Jerusalem, came down from God / God will dwell with his people / God will wipe away every tear / There will be no more death, sorrow or crying || Heart: What hope from Revelation 21 helps you face a hard season? || Mission: Encourage someone who is grieving this week with the promise of Revelation 21:4.

Question or prompt: The spies bring back a report
Notes: Key points: The spies returned after forty days / They showed the people the fruit of the land, including a cluster of grapes / The land flowed with milk and honey / The people there were giants, and the spies felt like grasshoppers / Caleb said they should go up and take the land || Heart: When fear makes you feel small, what truth about God helps you stand firm? || Mission: Speak one promise of God over a fear you have this week, and tell someone about it.

Question or prompt: The Shema
Notes: Key points: Hear, O Israel: the LORD our God is one LORD / Love the LORD with all your heart, soul and strength / These words are to be on your heart / Teach them diligently to your children / Talk of them when you sit, walk, lie down and rise / Write them on your doorposts and gates || Heart: How can your home become a place where God's words are spoken and lived? || Mission: Talk about one thing you have learned from the Bible with your family or a friend this week.

Question or prompt: Esther's courage
Notes: Key points: Mordecai told Esther about the plot against the Jews / Mordecai asked whether she came to the kingdom for such a time / Esther asked all the Jews to fast for three days / Esther decided to go in to the king / She said: if I perish, I perish || Heart: Where might God have placed you for such a time as this? || Mission: Pray this week for courage in one situation where you need to speak up for someone.

Question or prompt: The fiery furnace
Notes: Key points: Three friends refused to bow down to the golden image / The king threatened them with a burning fiery furnace / They said God was able to deliver them / A fourth figure, like the Son of God, walked with them in the fire / They came out, and the fire had no power over them || Heart: What would it mean to you to trust God even if he does not rescue you in the way you expect? || Mission: Stand firm this week in one small matter of faith, and tell a friend how God helped you.

Question or prompt: Nineveh repents
Notes: Key points: God told Jonah a second time to go to Nineveh / Jonah preached: yet forty days and Nineveh will be overthrown / The people of Nineveh believed God / The king covered himself with sackcloth and sat in ashes / God saw their works and relented of the evil || Heart: What does God's mercy towards Nineveh teach you about his heart for people you find hard to love? || Mission: Pray this week for someone you find difficult, and ask God to show you his mercy towards them.

Question or prompt: Job's response to loss
Notes: Key points: Job tore his robe and shaved his head / He fell down and worshipped / The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away / Blessed be the name of the LORD / In all this Job did not sin or charge God with wrong || Heart: How do you respond to God when life brings loss you did not expect? || Mission: Visit or call someone who is grieving this week, and simply listen.

Question or prompt: Trust in the LORD
Notes: Key points: Trust in the LORD with all your heart / Do not lean on your own understanding / In all your ways acknowledge him / He shall direct your paths / Do not be wise in your own eyes; fear the LORD and depart from evil || Heart: Where are you tempted to rely on your own understanding instead of trusting God? || Mission: Before one decision this week, ask God for direction in prayer, and write down what you sense.

Question or prompt: The fruit of the Spirit
Notes: Key points: The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy and peace / It also includes patience, kindness and goodness / Faith, meekness and self-control belong to it / Against such there is no law / Those who belong to Christ have crucified the flesh / If we live by the Spirit, let us also walk by the Spirit || Heart: Which fruit of the Spirit is growing in you, and which needs more of God's work? || Mission: Choose one fruit of the Spirit to practise this week, and tell a friend how you tried.

Question or prompt: Saved by grace
Notes: Key points: You are saved by grace through faith / This salvation is not of yourselves / It is the gift of God / Not of works, so that no one can boast / We are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works || Heart: How does knowing that salvation is a gift change the way you see your own efforts? || Mission: Thank God this week for one thing he has given you that you did not earn.

Question or prompt: Rejoice and do not be anxious
Notes: Key points: Rejoice in the Lord always / Let your gentleness be known to everyone / Be careful for nothing / Make your requests known by prayer and thanksgiving / The peace of God passes all understanding || Heart: What worry is God asking you to bring to him in prayer today? || Mission: Write down three things you are thankful for each day this week, and pray with thanksgiving.

Question or prompt: Faith described
Notes: Key points: Faith is the substance of things hoped for / By faith Abel offered a better sacrifice than Cain / Enoch was taken away and did not see death / By faith Noah prepared an ark / Without faith it is impossible to please God / God is a rewarder of those who seek him || Heart: What is one thing you are trusting God for that you cannot yet see? || Mission: Take one faithful step this week towards something you believe God has asked you to do.

Question or prompt: Trials and wisdom
Notes: Key points: Count it all joy when you meet trials / The trying of your faith works patience / If you lack wisdom, ask God, who gives liberally / Ask in faith, with no doubting / A double-minded man is unstable in all his ways || Heart: What trial is teaching you patience or wisdom right now? || Mission: Ask God this week for wisdom about one decision, and share your prayer with a friend.

Question or prompt: A chosen people
Notes: Key points: You are a chosen generation / You are a royal priesthood / You are a holy nation and a peculiar people / You should show forth the praises of God / You who were not a people are now the people of God || Heart: What does it mean to you to be called out of darkness into God's light? || Mission: Tell someone this week about God's mercy in your life, using 1 Peter 2:9.

Question or prompt: The Lord's Prayer
Notes: Key points: Jesus taught his disciples to pray to Our Father in heaven / Hallowed be your name, your kingdom come, your will done / Give us today our daily bread / Forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors / Lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil || Heart: Which line of the Lord's Prayer do you most need today? || Mission: Pray the Lord's Prayer slowly once a day this week, and pause on the line that speaks to you.

Question or prompt: The vine and the branches
Notes: Key points: Jesus says he is the true vine / His Father is the husbandman who takes care of the vine / Every branch that bears fruit is pruned to bear more / A branch cannot bear fruit unless it abides in the vine / Without me you can do nothing || Heart: What helps you to stay connected to Jesus in busy weeks? || Mission: Spend time this week reading John 15 with a friend, and talk about what it means to bear fruit.

Question or prompt: Pentecost
Notes: Key points: The disciples were all together in one place / A sound like a rushing wind filled the house / Tongues like fire sat upon each of them / They were filled with the Holy Ghost and spoke in other tongues / Some mocked, saying they were full of new wine || Heart: How would you describe the work of the Holy Spirit in your own life? || Mission: Pray this week for the boldness of the Holy Spirit to share your faith with one person.

Question or prompt: Bartimaeus receives his sight
Notes: Key points: Blind Bartimaeus sat by the road outside Jericho / He heard that Jesus of Nazareth was passing by / He cried out, Son of David, have mercy on me / Many told him to be quiet, but he cried all the more / Jesus asked what he wanted, and he received his sight || Heart: What do you need to ask Jesus for, even if others tell you to be quiet? || Mission: Make a specific prayer request this week, and keep asking for it until God answers.

Question or prompt: The Day of Atonement
Notes: Key points: Aaron's two sons died when they drew near before the LORD / Aaron must not come into the holy place at all times, behind the veil / Aaron cast lots over two goats / One goat was the scapegoat sent into the wilderness / The other goat was offered as a sin offering || Heart: What does the Day of Atonement teach you about the cost of sin and the grace of God? || Mission: Thank God this week for the atonement made through Jesus, and tell someone what it means to you.

Question or prompt: Elijah is taken up
Notes: Key points: The LORD was about to take Elijah up into heaven / Elisha refused to leave Elijah / A chariot of fire and horses of fire appeared / Elijah went up by a whirlwind / Elijah's mantle fell, and Elisha asked for a double portion || Heart: Who has God used in your life to pass on faith to you, and whom are you now mentoring? || Mission: Ask an older believer this week how they keep their faith strong, and write down one thing you learn.

Question or prompt: Give thanks to the LORD
Notes: Key points: Give thanks unto the LORD and call upon his name / Make known his deeds among the people / Sing unto him and talk of all his wondrous works / Glory in his holy name / Seek the LORD and his strength, and seek his face evermore || Heart: Which of God's works in your life do you most want to remember and tell others about? || Mission: Give thanks aloud this week for three specific things God has done, and share one with a friend.

Question or prompt: Jehoshaphat's prayer
Notes: Key points: Moab, Ammon and others came to fight against Jehoshaphat / Jehoshaphat feared and set himself to seek the LORD / Judah gathered to ask help from the LORD and fasted / He prayed: we have no might against this great company / The LORD said the battle is not yours but God's || Heart: When you face a battle you cannot win alone, what do you do first? || Mission: Make a prayer of trust this week, like Jehoshaphat's, about a challenge you face.

Question or prompt: Ezra prepares his heart
Notes: Key points: Ezra was a ready scribe in the law of Moses / The hand of the LORD his God was upon him / He had prepared his heart to seek the law of the LORD / He was determined to do it and to teach the statutes / The king granted him all he requested || Heart: What does it mean to prepare your heart before you study God's Word? || Mission: Before you read the Bible this week, pray for your heart to be ready, and write down what God shows you.

Question or prompt: Nehemiah's prayer
Notes: Key points: Nehemiah heard that the walls of Jerusalem were broken down / He sat down, wept, and mourned for days / He fasted and prayed before the God of heaven / He confessed the sins of Israel, including his own / He asked God for mercy and success before the king || Heart: What burden on your heart could you bring to God in prayer, as Nehemiah did? || Mission: Pray for the rebuilding of a broken place in your community this week, and do one practical thing to help.

Question or prompt: Remember your Creator
Notes: Key points: Remember now your Creator in the days of your youth / The evil days come, when there is no pleasure in them / The dust returns to the earth, and the spirit to God / God will bring every work into judgment / Fear God and keep his commandments; this is the whole duty of man || Heart: What would it mean for you to remember God now, not later? || Mission: Set one daily habit this week that keeps God first, and review it at the end of the week.

Question or prompt: The voice of the beloved
Notes: Key points: The beloved comes leaping upon the mountains / He is like a roe or a young hart / The winter is past, and the rain is over and gone / The flowers appear on the earth and the time of singing is come / The voice of the turtle is heard in the land || Heart: How does this love song speak to you about the joy of God's love? || Mission: Thank God this week for a relationship that brings you joy, and encourage the people in it.

Question or prompt: Jeremiah is called
Notes: Key points: The word of the LORD came to Jeremiah / God knew Jeremiah before he was formed / God ordained him a prophet to the nations / Jeremiah said: I cannot speak, for I am a child / God touched his mouth and put his words in it || Heart: Where do you feel too young or unready for God's call, and what does his answer tell you? || Mission: Say yes to one small way God has been asking you to serve this month.

Question or prompt: Great is thy faithfulness
Notes: Key points: Remember the affliction and the gall / The soul is humbled within / The LORD's mercies are new every morning / Great is his faithfulness / The LORD is my portion, therefore I will hope in him || Heart: What hope from Lamentations 3 helps you face a hard day? || Mission: Each morning this week, read Lamentations 3:22-23 and thank God for his mercies that day.

Question or prompt: The valley of dry bones
Notes: Key points: Ezekiel was set down in a valley full of bones / The bones were very dry / God asked: can these bones live? / Ezekiel prophesied to the bones, as he was told / Breath came into them and they lived, a great army || Heart: Where in your life or community do you need God to breathe new life? || Mission: Pray this week for someone or something that feels dry, and ask God to bring life to it.

Question or prompt: God woos his people
Notes: Key points: God will allure Israel and bring her into the wilderness / The valley of Achor will be a door of hope / God will betroth Israel to himself forever / In righteousness, judgment, mercy and faithfulness / God will say to them: Ye are my people || Heart: How does God's faithfulness, even when we fail, change the way you come back to him? || Mission: Write a short letter of return to God this week, and read it aloud as a prayer.

Question or prompt: Return to the LORD
Notes: Key points: Turn to me with all your heart, with fasting and weeping / Rend your heart and not your garments / The LORD is gracious and merciful / He is slow to anger and of great kindness / He repents of the evil || Heart: Is there a sin you have been dressing up on the outside that God wants you to deal with inside? || Mission: Confess one area of heart-change to God this week, and make one practical change that shows it.

Question or prompt: Seek good and live
Notes: Key points: Seek good, and not evil, that you may live / So the LORD God of hosts shall be with you / Hate the evil and love the good / Establish judgment in the gate / It may be the LORD will be gracious to the remnant || Heart: Where does God call you to choose good over evil in your daily choices? || Mission: Stand up for justice in one small way this week, in your home, school or workplace.

Question or prompt: The day of the LORD
Notes: Key points: The day of the LORD is near upon all the heathen / As you have done, it shall be done to you / Deliverance shall be on mount Zion / The house of Jacob shall be a fire / The kingdom shall be the LORD's || Heart: What does Obadiah teach you about pride, and about the justice of God? || Mission: Pray this week for anyone who has wronged you, and ask God to deal with the matter as he sees fit.

Question or prompt: What does the LORD require?
Notes: Key points: Wherewith shall I come before the LORD? / Shall I come with burnt offerings, thousands of rams? / God has shown you what is good: to do justly / To love mercy / To walk humbly with your God || Heart: Which of the three, justice, mercy or humility, do you find hardest to practise? || Mission: Choose one way to do justly and love mercy this week, and tell a friend about it.

Question or prompt: The LORD is good
Notes: Key points: The LORD is jealous and revengeth / The LORD is slow to anger and great in power / The clouds are the dust of his feet / The LORD is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble / He knoweth them that trust in him || Heart: Which quality of God in this passage gives you the most security in a time of trouble? || Mission: Write down a trouble you face, and pray Nahum 1:7 over it each day this week.

Question or prompt: Write the vision
Notes: Key points: God told Habakkuk to write the vision and make it plain / Though it tarry, wait for it / The just shall live by his faith / The proud man's soul is not upright in him / The vision will surely come || Heart: Where are you waiting on God, and what does it mean to live by faith while you wait? || Mission: Write down a vision or promise God has given you, and review it with a friend this week.

Question or prompt: Sing, O daughter of Zion
Notes: Key points: Sing, O daughter of Zion / The LORD has taken away the judgments against you / The King of Israel is in the midst of you / You shall not see evil any more / He will rest in his love and rejoice over you with singing || Heart: What does it mean to you that God rejoices over you with singing? || Mission: Sing a song of praise this week, and let it remind you that God delights in you.

Question or prompt: Consider your ways
Notes: Key points: The people said: the time is not come to build the LORD's house / Consider your ways / You looked for much, and it came to little / Go up to the mountain, bring wood, and build the house / I will take pleasure in it, and I will be glorified || Heart: Where are you putting your own comfort before God's work? || Mission: Give time or money this week to a project that builds up God's work, and reflect on it.

Question or prompt: Not by might, nor by power
Notes: Key points: Not by might nor by power, but by my Spirit, says the LORD / Who has despised the day of small things? / The seven eyes of the LORD rejoice to see the plummet / Zerubbabel's hands shall finish the house / You shall know that the LORD has sent me || Heart: Where are you tempted to measure God's work by its size, rather than by his Spirit? || Mission: Serve in a small way this week, and thank God for the day of small things.

Question or prompt: Bring all the tithes
Notes: Key points: Will a man rob God? Ye have robbed me in tithes and offerings / Bring all the tithes into the storehouse / Prove me now, says the LORD of hosts / I will open the windows of heaven / I will rebuke the devourer, and all nations shall call you blessed || Heart: What does generous giving show about your trust in God? || Mission: Decide on one act of generosity this month, and invite God to show you his faithfulness through it.

Question or prompt: Love is patient
Notes: Key points: Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels / Though I have all faith, but have not charity, I am nothing / Charity suffereth long and is kind / It envieth not, vaunteth not itself / Beareth all things, believeth all things, endureth all things || Heart: Which quality of love in 1 Corinthians 13 would most change your home or friendships? || Mission: Show patient, kind love to someone who is difficult this week, and note what you learn.

Question or prompt: A new creation
Notes: Key points: If any man be in Christ, he is a new creature / Old things are passed away; all things become new / God has given us the ministry of reconciliation / We are ambassadors for Christ / He made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin || Heart: What old habit or fear is God inviting you to let go of, now that you are new in Christ? || Mission: Be an ambassador of reconciliation this week: pray for and reach out to someone you are at odds with.

Question or prompt: Clothe yourselves
Notes: Key points: Put on bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind / Put on meekness and longsuffering / Forbearing one another and forgiving / Above all, put on charity, which is the bond of perfectness / Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly || Heart: Which quality in Colossians 3 do you most need to put on this week? || Mission: Memorise Colossians 3:12 and practise one of its qualities with someone this week.

Question or prompt: Rejoice, pray, give thanks
Notes: Key points: Rejoice evermore / Pray without ceasing / In every thing give thanks / Quench not the Spirit / Despise not prophesyings; prove all things, hold fast what is good || Heart: Which of the three, rejoicing, praying or giving thanks, is hardest for you right now? || Mission: Give thanks in everything this week, and keep a note of what you are thankful for.

Question or prompt: Work quietly and do not grow weary
Notes: Key points: Withdraw from every brother who walks disorderly / If any would not work, neither should he eat / Work with quietness and eat your own bread / Be not weary in well doing / If anyone does not obey, note that man and do not keep company with him || Heart: How does honest, steady work reflect your faith to the people around you? || Mission: Finish one piece of work this week with care, as an offering to God, and do not grow weary in doing good.

Question or prompt: An example to believers
Notes: Key points: Let no man despise your youth; be an example in word, conversation and purity / Give attendance to reading, exhortation and doctrine / Neglect not the gift that is in you / Meditate upon these things; give thyself wholly to them / Take heed to yourself and to the doctrine; in doing this you shall save yourself and them || Heart: In what way can you be an example to others, whatever your age? || Mission: Choose one way this week to set an example in speech, love, faith or purity, and ask a friend to notice.

Question or prompt: Stir up the gift of God
Notes: Key points: Paul remembers Timothy in his prayers night and day / The unfeigned faith that dwelt first in your grandmother and mother / Stir up the gift of God that is in you / God has not given us the spirit of fear, but of power, love and a sound mind / Be not ashamed of the testimony of our Lord || Heart: What gift has God given you that you have not yet used fully? || Mission: Use one of your gifts this week to encourage someone, and pray for courage to do it boldly.

Question or prompt: The grace that teaches
Notes: Key points: The grace of God that brings salvation has appeared to all men / It teaches us to deny ungodliness and worldly lusts / We should live soberly, righteously and godly / We look for the blessed hope and glorious appearing / He gave himself to redeem us from all iniquity || Heart: What does God's grace teach you to say no to, and to say yes to? || Mission: Name one habit you will say no to this week, and one good work you will say yes to.

Question or prompt: The love and faith of Philemon
Notes: Key points: Paul thanks God for Philemon, making mention of him in his prayers / Paul hears of Philemon's love and faith towards the Lord Jesus / The bowels of the saints are refreshed by Philemon / Paul has much joy and consolation in his love / Paul asks Philemon to receive a brother back || Heart: How can your love and faith refresh the people of God around you? || Mission: Refresh someone in your church or family this week with a note, a visit or a prayer.

Question or prompt: Add to your faith
Notes: Key points: God has given us exceeding great and precious promises / We may be partakers of the divine nature / Add to your faith virtue, knowledge, temperance / Add patience, godliness, brotherly kindness and charity / Make your calling and election sure || Heart: Which step in 2 Peter 1 is your next step of growth? || Mission: Choose one quality from 2 Peter 1 to grow in this week, and ask a friend to pray with you about it.

Question or prompt: Walking in the light
Notes: Key points: God is light, and in him is no darkness at all / If we say we have fellowship with him and walk in darkness, we lie / If we walk in the light, we have fellowship one with another / The blood of Jesus cleanseth us from all sin / If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive || Heart: Is there something hidden that you need to bring into the light and confess? || Mission: Confess something to God this week, and find a trusted friend who can pray with you.

Question or prompt: Walk in truth and love
Notes: Key points: John rejoiced that some walk in truth / He wrote not a new commandment, but one from the beginning / That we love one another / This is love, that we walk after his commandments / This is the commandment, that as you have heard from the beginning, you should walk in it || Heart: How does walking in truth and love connect for you? || Mission: Walk in truth and love with one person this week: be honest and kind, both at once.

Question or prompt: Walk in the truth
Notes: Key points: John prays that Gaius may prosper and be in health / John rejoiced greatly when the brethren came and testified of his truth / John has no greater joy than to hear that his children walk in truth / Gaius has done faithfully whatever he did to the brethren and strangers / We ought therefore to receive such, that we might be fellowhelpers to the truth || Heart: How do you welcome and support fellow believers, especially those you do not know well? || Mission: Welcome a visitor or a new believer this week, and help them feel at home.

Question or prompt: Keep yourselves in the love of God
Notes: Key points: Build yourselves up on your most holy faith / Pray in the Holy Ghost / Keep yourselves in the love of God / Look for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ / He is able to keep you from falling and present you faultless || Heart: What helps you keep your footing in faith when the world pulls you off course? || Mission: Build yourself up this week: read Jude 20-21 each morning and pray in the Spirit for a friend.

Question or prompt: I was a Jewish woman raised by my cousin in a foreign land.
Notes: Esther risked her life to plead with the king for her people.

Question or prompt: I was chosen to become queen of a great Persian king.
At first I did not reveal who my people were.
My cousin asked me to plead with the king for my people.
I said: 'If I perish, I perish.' Who am I?
I was born when the king of Egypt ordered baby boys to be killed.
Notes: Moses led the people out of Egypt and received the law on Mount Sinai.

Question or prompt: My mother hid me in a basket among the reeds of the river.
Pharaoh's daughter found me and raised me in the palace.
God spoke to me from a burning bush.
I led my people out of Egypt and received the law on a mountain. Who am I?
I was a Moabite woman who married into an Israelite family.
Notes: Ruth's loyalty to Naomi led to a place in the line of King David.

Question or prompt: After my husband died, I stayed with my mother-in-law.
I went out to gather grain in the fields to provide for us.
I became the great-grandmother of King David. Who am I?
I was taken as a young man from Judah to serve in Babylon.
Notes: Daniel was faithful to God in Babylon, even in the lions' den.

Question or prompt: I refused to eat the king's food and chose vegetables and water.
I interpreted the king's dreams.
I was thrown into a den of lions.
God shut the mouths of the lions. Who am I?
I was the sister of Moses and Aaron.
Notes: Miriam watched over her baby brother and led the women in song after the Red Sea.

Question or prompt: I watched over my baby brother when he was placed in the river.
I was a prophetess who led the women in song.
After the Red Sea I sang and danced with a tambourine.
I spoke against Moses and was struck with a skin disease. Who am I?

Question or prompt: Passover and the Red Sea

Question or prompt: Jonah and the great fish

Question or prompt: Daniel in the lions' den

Question or prompt: The twelve spies

Notes: Heart: When fear speaks louder than God's promise, whose voice do you listen to? || Mission: Speak one faithful word this week, even if others see things differently.

Question or prompt: Jericho falls
Answer: Rahab hides two spies on her roof / She makes a promise with the spies and ties a scarlet cord in her window / Israel crosses the Jordan on dry ground and marches around Jericho / The walls fall down, and Rahab and her family are saved
Notes: Heart: What does Rahab's courage teach you about trusting God's promises? || Mission: Show courage this week by keeping a promise, even when it is costly.

Question or prompt: Gideon and the three hundred
Answer: Gideon threshes wheat in a winepress to hide from Midian / God calls him a mighty man of valour and asks him to save Israel / Gideon reduces his army to three hundred men / They break the pitchers, blow the trumpets, and the enemy flees
Notes: Heart: Where might God be asking you to trust him with less, so that he gets the glory? || Mission: Do one task this week that depends on God's strength rather than your own resources.

Question or prompt: Ruth and Boaz
Answer: Ruth stays with Naomi and goes to Bethlehem with her / Ruth gleans in the field of Boaz / Boaz redeems the family land and marries Ruth / Their son Obed becomes the grandfather of King David
Notes: Heart: How has God shown his faithfulness to you through the kindness of others? || Mission: Show kindness to someone who is a stranger or in need this week.

Question or prompt: David and Goliath
Answer: The Philistines gather for battle, and Goliath challenges Israel / David, a young shepherd, comes with a sling and five smooth stones / David says the battle is the LORD's / A stone from the sling strikes Goliath, and David wins
Notes: Heart: What giant in your life needs you to trust God's strength rather than your own? || Mission: Take on one challenge this week that you have been avoiding, trusting God to help you.

Question or prompt: David and Bathsheba
Answer: David stays in Jerusalem while his army goes to war / He sees Bathsheba bathing and sends for her / He arranges for Uriah to die in battle / Nathan confronts David, who confesses: I have sinned against the LORD
Notes: Heart: What does David's confession teach you about how to respond when you are found out? || Mission: Confess one hidden fault to God this week, and seek the help of a trusted friend.

Question or prompt: Elijah on Mount Carmel
Answer: Elijah challenges the prophets of Baal to a contest on Mount Carmel / The prophets of Baal cry out all day, but no answer comes / Elijah repairs the altar of the LORD and pours water over the sacrifice / Fire falls from heaven, and the people say: The LORD, he is God
Notes: Heart: Whom are you serving, and how would you know if your devotion is real? || Mission: Remove one idol from your life this week, and set time aside to worship the LORD alone.

Question or prompt: Naaman is healed
Answer: Naaman, a commander of Syria, is a leper / A young Israelite girl tells him of the prophet Elisha / Elisha tells him to wash seven times in the Jordan / Naaman obeys, is healed, and praises the God of Israel
Notes: Heart: What pride might stop you from doing a simple thing God asks of you? || Mission: Do the simple thing God has been asking you to do this week, and be humble about it.

Question or prompt: David brings the ark home
Answer: David gathers all Israel to bring the ark of God to Jerusalem / The Levites carry the ark on their shoulders, as the law commanded / David dances before the LORD with all his might / David appoints Levites to thank, praise and sing before the ark
Notes: Heart: How do you express joy in worship, even when it is not what others expect? || Mission: Give thanks and sing praise to God this week, aloud or in your heart, every day.

Question or prompt: Solomon builds the temple
Answer: Solomon prepares to build a house for the name of the LORD / He asks Huram of Tyre for cedar and skilled craftsmen / The temple is finished and the ark is brought into the Most Holy Place / The glory of the LORD fills the house, and the people worship
Notes: Heart: What would it mean for your life to be a house in which God's presence dwells? || Mission: Prepare a place in your home or church for prayer and worship this week, and use it daily.

Question or prompt: The return and the rebuilding
Answer: Cyrus, king of Persia, lets the exiles go home to Jerusalem / The people return and build the altar, then the foundation of the temple / Opponents try to stop the work, and it stops for years / Haggai and Zechariah encourage the people, and the temple is finished
Notes: Heart: When has discouragement made you stop building what God has asked you to build? || Mission: Return to one piece of unfinished work this week, and ask God for encouragement to finish it.

Question or prompt: Rebuilding the walls
Answer: Nehemiah hears that Jerusalem's walls are broken and prays / The king sends him to Jerusalem to rebuild the walls / Opponents mock and threaten, but the people keep working with a sword in one hand / The wall is finished in fifty-two days, and the enemies see that God has done it
Notes: Heart: What wall in your life or community needs rebuilding, and who could help you? || Mission: Join or start one practical act of service this week, and pray for the people you serve.

Question or prompt: Esther speaks for her people
Answer: Haman plots to destroy the Jews, and Mordecai asks Esther to act / Esther fasts, then goes in to the king without being called / She invites the king and Haman to a banquet, then asks for her people's lives / The king gives the Jews the right to defend themselves, and Haman is hanged
Notes: Heart: Where has God placed you for a time such as this, and what courage does it require? || Mission: Speak up this week for someone who is being treated unjustly, in a way that is wise and kind.

Question or prompt: Job's trial and restoration
Answer: Job is blameless and upright, and he loses his children and wealth / His friends come to comfort him, and they sit silent with him for seven days / Job questions God, and then bows in worship: I have heard of thee / God restores Job, giving him twice as much as he had before
Notes: Heart: What does Job teach you about trusting God when the reason for your suffering is unclear? || Mission: Pray honestly this week, bringing your questions to God, and listen for his answer in Scripture.

Question or prompt: Jesus walks on the water
Answer: The disciples are in a boat, tossed by the waves, and afraid / Jesus comes to them walking on the sea and says: Be of good cheer / Peter asks to come to Jesus, and steps out of the boat onto the water / Peter sinks, cries out, and Jesus lifts him up; the storm ceases
Notes: Heart: When have you been afraid, and how did Jesus meet you in that fear? || Mission: Take one step of faith this week, and call on Jesus when you begin to sink.

Question or prompt: Jairus's daughter and the woman
Answer: Jairus begs Jesus to come and heal his dying daughter / On the way, a woman who has bled for twelve years touches his clothes and is healed / Jesus asks who touched him, and the woman comes trembling and tells the truth / Jesus raises Jairus's daughter, saying: Be not afraid, only believe
Notes: Heart: Where do you need to come to Jesus with courage, even if you feel small or unseen? || Mission: Bring a need to Jesus in prayer this week, and be honest with him about it.

Question or prompt: The man born blind
Answer: Jesus sees a man who has been blind from birth / Jesus makes clay from spittle, anoints his eyes, and sends him to wash in Siloam / The man comes back seeing, and his neighbours and the Pharisees question him / He answers: One thing I know, that, whereas I was blind, now I see
Notes: Heart: How has Jesus given you sight in an area where you were once blind? || Mission: Tell someone this week what Jesus has done in your life, in one honest sentence.

Question or prompt: Paul and Silas in Philippi
Answer: Paul casts an evil spirit out of a slave girl, and her owners drag them before the magistrates / Paul and Silas are beaten and put in the inner prison with their feet in stocks / At midnight they pray and sing hymns, and an earthquake opens the doors / The jailer asks what he must do to be saved, and his whole household believes
Notes: Heart: How might God use your suffering to bring someone else to faith? || Mission: Pray and sing praise this week in a difficult situation, and share your faith with one person.
